content.title: About
content.content: Alfredo sauce with meat is a creamy sauce made from butter, cream, and Parmesan cheese, enriched with pieces of cooked meat (commonly chicken, beef, or pork). It has a smooth, slightly nutty flavor and a thick texture, perfect for pasta, risotto, and casseroles.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The classic Alfredo sauce was created in the early 1920s at the Alfredo restaurant in Rome.
The original recipe contained only butter, cream, and Parmesan, without any meat.
Adding meat makes the sauce more filling and boosts its protein content.
In American cuisine the sauce is often used as a base for "chicken Alfredo" and "seafood Alfredo" dishes.
There are many variations of the sauce, including mushroom, spinach, bacon, and other ingredient additions.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Parmesan cheese and cream provide a good amount of calcium, essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: The meat adds complete proteins that support tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Meat and dairy are excellent sources of vitamin B12, important for nerve function and blood formation.

items.title: Provides vitamin A
items.content: Cream and cheese contain provitamin A (beta‑carotene) that converts to vitamin A, supporting vision.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The sauce supplies quick energy through its fat and carbohydrate content.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Butter and cream make the sauce calorie‑dense; excessive intake may contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Lactose
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience discomfort after consuming the sauce.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Parmesan adds salt, so those monitoring sodium should keep portions moderate.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Allergy to milk or cheese can trigger reactions when eating the sauce.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the sauce hot over pasta (fettuccine, spaghetti), rice, mashed potatoes, or in casseroles. It can be tossed with sautéed vegetables for a quick one‑pan meal. Garnish with fresh herbs or extra grated Parmesan before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the sauce in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags for up to 2 months. Reheat gently over low heat while stirring to prevent separation.
